doc.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002

title: Jerome Richardson's quartet around 1953
summary: With the Black Hawk cutting back, he works Sundays and with Richardson's quartet at the Village in Richmond; Rowe mentions Richardson.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Well I’ve been lucky. Just blessed, blessed. Then many times I get a break. The drummers would come in. Shelly Manne, Max came in, by then I had left, I was with Fatha Hines and I went down on the jam session, or went down on the performance night to see Max. Because hell he was the man. And a fella named George Morrow was playing bass with him, well George Morrow, we had played together with the Jerome Richardson quartet. See Jerome Richardson’s quartet, see they started cutting back at the Black Hawk. That was in around 1953. And so they would just hire me just for Sundays only.

Or when a name came in and they wanted to augment the band. Maybe it was ’52, ’53. So I went to work with Jerome. Jerome Richardson. He had a little quartet and he was struggling so he did three or four nights maybe here or three or four nights there. So with Jerome we played a place called The Village in Richmond and we had George Morrow and Jerome and Cedrick Haywood on piano.
Well you and I have something in common then.
Two summers ago I recorded an album and Jerome Richardson played on it.
It might have been three summers now that I come to think of it.
